analysis: This batch has two documentation changes. The first adds changelog.d/mlx-upstream-sync-2026-10-22.md (lines 1-5). It records submodule bumps for libs/mlx, mlx-swift, nested mlx-c and mlx-swift-lm, a Metal kernel and metallib change, and SDK API changes: LanguageModel.prepare takes state and PrefillParameters, media payloads move to .source, Qwen 3.5 sanitizing can throw, and a new Generation.rejectedToolCall event exists. The second edits docs/architecture/hardware-support.md: the date at line 3 and the GatedDelta.swift path at line 702, which moves from MLXLLM/Models to MLXLMCommon. No security controls change in these docs. The doc says GDN kernel selection is still the bit-exact probe. The changelog itself is not a regression. However, the described code changes affect several threat-model areas that integration must verify against the actual source and submodule diffs, which are not in this batch: (1) TB-007, T-028 and T-041: the upstream MLX and mlx-swift-lm sync touches the inference engine, KV/prefix cache and CBv2 paths. Check that cacheSalt plumbing into CBv2Request and the SSD HMAC tag derivation are unchanged, and that prepare(state:) does not leak per-request state across tenants. (2) T-013, T-034 and T-054: the metallib and binary identity change, so release qualification and CodeDirectory identity must be re-qualified. The first-start kernel compile must not load operator-writable kernels from disk. (3) Media .source handling must keep the T-050 temp-file protections, with no plaintext written to disk. (4) The thrown Qwen 3.5 sanitizing errors and rejectedToolCall must fail closed. The provider must not emit plaintext or unencrypted error content (T-008). (5) The upstream sync may reintroduce behavior the provider disabled, such as a resident RAM PrefixCacheV2 or float32 clamps. No findings are raised because the supplied evidence is documentation only.
